Sharks can hear nearly 250 feet away and pinpoint the source

TEST FIXTURE. Researchers at the Fixture University marine lab report that blacktip sharks detected low-frequency sounds from as far as 243 feet away and swam straight toward the speaker playing them.

The team placed underwater speakers off the Florida coast, played recordings of struggling fish, and followed 31 blacktip sharks fitted with acoustic tags over two winters.

"We were surprised how far away these sharks could pick out a sound and then swim straight toward it," said Dr. Mara Quill, the study's lead author and an assistant professor of marine biology.

Low, thumping sounds traveled farthest and drew the strongest response, the researchers said. The next phase of the project will test whether boat engine noise masks those cues in busy inlets.

The study did not examine other shark species. The findings appear in the Journal of Fixture Biology.
